ROLE: reporter
You write the final diagnosis of an incident from the evidence gathered. Every statement must be backed by evidence IDs taken from the evidence list; never invent an ID.

Root-cause categories (root_cause_category must be exactly one of these):
- bad_deployment: a new release introduced a defect (errors begin right after a deploy)
- db_connection_pool_exhaustion: every database connection in the pool is in use, so requests wait
- slow_query_missing_index: a database query became slow (for example a missing index)
- downstream_timeout: a dependency the service calls is slow or unresponsive
- memory_leak_oom: memory grows until the process is killed (OOM) and restarts
- disk_full: a volume is full so writes fail
- expired_tls_cert: a TLS certificate expired so handshakes fail
- misconfiguration: a wrong environment variable, setting or feature flag
- traffic_spike_rate_limit: request volume far above capacity, causing rate limiting or load shedding
- cache_stampede_outage: the cache is down or emptied so everything falls through to the database

Rules:
- claims: factual statements about what the evidence shows. Each cites one or more evidence IDs (log lines L-..., metrics M-..., runbook sections R-...) that actually support it.
- recommended_actions: concrete next steps for the on-call engineer, taken from the retrieved runbook sections. Each cites at least one runbook section ID (R-...).
- ruled_out: other hypotheses you considered and rejected, as short strings.
- confidence: low, medium or high.

Reply with only JSON in this shape:
{"incident_id": "INC-001", "root_cause_category": "disk_full", "root_cause_summary": "one or two sentences", "confidence": "high", "claims": [{"statement": "...", "evidence_ids": ["L-0123", "M-021"]}], "recommended_actions": [{"statement": "...", "evidence_ids": ["R-06-5"]}], "ruled_out": ["..."]}

Alert: inventory-service: HTTP error rate above 5% for 5 minutes (since 21:42 UTC)
Alerting service: inventory
Alert time: 2026-03-08T21:42:00Z
Data available from 2026-03-08T20:00:00Z to 2026-03-08T23:00:00Z

Evidence:
Step 1: metrics_query {"aggregation": "max", "end": "2026-03-08T22:00:00Z", "metric": "error_rate_pct", "service": "inventory", "start": "2026-03-08T21:30:00Z"} (asked because: Check the magnitude and timing of the error rate spike on the inventory service.)
  Result: M-023: Only 7 points in this range, too few to test for a change; use a wider range.
  [M-023] inventory.error_rate_pct from 2026-03-08T21:30:00Z to 2026-03-08T22:00:00Z (7 points, 5-minute steps): min=0.28 max=17.13 mean=12.25 last=17.13; max=17.13. Only 7 points in this range, too few to test for a change; use a wider range. Notable points: 2026-03-08T21:35:00Z = 0.28 (lowest); 2026-03-08T22:00:00Z = 17.13 (last); 2026-03-08T22:00:00Z = 17.13 (peak).
Step 2: log_search {"end": "2026-03-08T21:45:00Z", "level": "ERROR", "limit": 30, "query": "error,exception,failed,timeout", "service": "inventory", "start": "2026-03-08T21:35:00Z"} (asked because: Find error logs in the inventory service around the alert time to see what is failing.)
  Result: 4 matching log lines.
  [L-0296] 2026-03-08T21:41:56Z inventory ERROR request failed status=500 path=/api/v1/stock request_id=req-0a923eba duration_ms=3197
  [L-0305] 2026-03-08T21:43:54Z inventory ERROR request failed status=502 path=/api/v1/stock request_id=req-b9edbe08
  [L-0306] 2026-03-08T21:43:55Z inventory ERROR request failed status=502 path=/api/v1/stock request_id=req-daeec02f
  [L-0307] 2026-03-08T21:44:02Z inventory ERROR request failed status=502 path=/api/v1/stock request_id=req-c6b98ca5
Step 3: metrics_query {"aggregation": "max", "end": "2026-03-08T22:00:00Z", "metric": "db_pool_in_use_pct", "service": "inventory", "start": "2026-03-08T21:00:00Z"} (asked because: Check if database connection pool is exhausted on the inventory service.)
  Result: M-021: Change detected at 2026-03-08T21:15:00Z: mean 29.14 before, 67.97 after (29.1 baseline standard deviations).
  [M-021] inventory.db_pool_in_use_pct from 2026-03-08T21:00:00Z to 2026-03-08T22:00:00Z (13 points, 5-minute steps): min=27.25 max=100 mean=59.01 last=100; max=100. Change detected at 2026-03-08T21:15:00Z: mean 29.14 before, 67.97 after (29.1 baseline standard deviations). Notable points: 2026-03-08T21:10:00Z = 27.25 (lowest); 2026-03-08T21:15:00Z = 31.19 (first point after the change); 2026-03-08T21:55:00Z = 100 (peak); 2026-03-08T22:00:00Z = 100 (last).
Step 4: metrics_query {"aggregation": "max", "end": "2026-03-08T22:00:00Z", "metric": "latency_p99_ms", "service": "inventory", "start": "2026-03-08T21:00:00Z"} (asked because: Check p99 latency to confirm the slow response times leading to downstream timeouts.)
  Result: M-024: Change detected at 2026-03-08T21:15:00Z: mean 117.73 before, 3024.62 after (2229.6 baseline standard deviations).
  [M-024] inventory.latency_p99_ms from 2026-03-08T21:00:00Z to 2026-03-08T22:00:00Z (13 points, 5-minute steps): min=116 max=6567.91 mean=2353.8 last=6567.91; max=6567.91. Change detected at 2026-03-08T21:15:00Z: mean 117.73 before, 3024.62 after (2229.6 baseline standard deviations). Notable points: 2026-03-08T21:10:00Z = 116 (lowest); 2026-03-08T21:15:00Z = 122.24 (first point after the change); 2026-03-08T22:00:00Z = 6567.91 (last); 2026-03-08T22:00:00Z = 6567.91 (peak).
Step 5: runbook_retrieve {"k": 3, "query": "database connection pool exhaustion pool_in_use_pct high latency"} (asked because: Retrieve runbook guidance and mitigation steps for database connection pool exhaustion.)
  Result: 3 runbook sections; best match R-03-8 (match score 12.6).
  [R-03-8] Slow query or missing index - Related runbooks (match score 12.6): If queries are quick but requests wait for connections, use the pool exhaustion runbook. If the database is overloaded because the cache failed, use the cache runbook. If pool use rises slowly over days instead, use the connection leak audit.
  [R-02-3] Database connection pool exhaustion - How to confirm (match score 10.9): Check how much of the connection pool is in use: it sits at or very near its maximum. Look for log lines saying a connection is not available or that the pool is exhausted, with many requests waiting. Then look at individual queries: if they are quick and the delay is the wait for a connection, this is pool exhaustion.
  [R-12-8] Database connection leak audit - Related runbooks (match score 10.5): For an acute outage with all connections in use, use the connection pool exhaustion runbook. For one very slow query, use the slow query runbook. This audit is only for slow drift, so do not start it during an incident.

Hypotheses from the investigation:
- db_connection_pool_exhaustion: Database connection pool usage reached 100%, which directly correlates with the massive spike in p99 latency and request failures starting around 21:15 UTC. (evidence: M-021, M-024, L-0296, L-0305, L-0306, L-0307, R-02-3)
- slow_query_missing_index: The connection pool exhaustion and high latency can be driven by a slow database query or missing index holding onto connections. (evidence: M-021, M-024, R-03-8)
